title: After three years of debate, one language was chosen to speak for an entire country.
sources: Wikipedia - Hindi Day (adoption of Hindi, 14 September 1949, Article 343)
Civilsdaily / Byju's - This Day in History, September 14 - Hindi Diwas and the Munshi-Ayyangar formula
caption:
After three years of debate, one language was chosen to speak for an entire country.

On September 14, 1949, India's Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi, written in Devanagari script, as the official language of the Union - Article 343 of the Constitution. The decision came through the Munshi-Ayyangar formula, a compromise built after nearly three years of debate.

India has never had a single native tongue - it has hundreds. Settling on Hindi for official Union business, while protecting the status of every other Indian language, took genuine negotiation, not just a vote.

September 14th is observed nationwide as Hindi Diwas - a reminder that even a country's most basic administrative choices, like which language runs its government, had to be built through compromise, not assumed.
